subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
description: A quick, practical guide to Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion.

hook.text: Johannes Kepler discovered that planets orbit in ellipses, not circles. It took him years of calculation to prove it.

buildup.text: Using Tycho's data, Kepler tried circular orbits first. They didn't fit Mars by 8 arc-minutes—and he refused to ignore it.

discovery.text: His three laws describe how planets move: elliptical orbits, equal areas in equal times, and a period-distance relationship.

twist.text: Kepler was motivated by mysticism—he believed God designed the cosmos with geometric harmony. His math outlasted his theology.

climax.text: Newton later showed Kepler's laws follow directly from gravity. Kepler described the motion; Newton explained why.

punchline.text: Eight arc-minutes of error. Kepler refused to ignore it and found the truth.

quiz.question: What did Kepler discover about planetary orbits?
options: They are ellipses, not perfect circles
They are perfect circles centered on the Sun
They follow random paths influenced by other planets

details.summary: Johannes Kepler discovered that planets move in ellipses (not circles) with the Sun at one focus, sweep equal areas in equal times (moving faster when closer to the Sun), and that orbital period squared equals semi-major axis cubed.
details.whyItMatters: Kepler's laws were the first accurate mathematical description of planetary motion. They demolished 2,000 years of circular-orbit dogma and provided the empirical foundation that Newton later explained with universal gravitation.
takeaways: Planets orbit in ellipses with the Sun at one focus
They sweep equal areas in equal times during their orbit
Orbital period squared equals semi-major axis cubed

faq.question: How did Kepler discover elliptical orbits?
faq.answer: Using Tycho Brahe's precise Mars observations, Kepler spent years trying to fit circular orbits. An 8-arcminute discrepancy — tiny but bigger than Tycho's measurement error — refused to go away.

faq.question: Did Kepler know why planets move in ellipses?
faq.answer: No. He described how planets move but couldn't explain why. He speculated about magnetic forces from the Sun.
